'''Mark Luitzen Brongersma''' (born 1969), is a Dutch physicist and [[Materials science|materials scientist]] specializing in [[nanophotonics]], [[plasmonics]], [[metamaterials]], and [[optoelectronics]]. He is the Stephen Harris Professor of Materials Science and Engineering and a professor, by courtesy, of Applied Physics at [[Stanford University]].<ref name=stanford>{{cite web |title=Mark Brongersma |url=https://profiles.stanford.edu/mark-brongersma |website=Stanford Profiles |access-date=May 14, 2025}}</ref> Brongersma has worked in the fields of nanophotonics and plasmonics, having coined the terms "plasmonics" and "Mie-tronics", and has made contributions to the development of optical metasurfaces and atomically thin optics.<ref name=optica>{{cite web |title=Mark Brongersma |url=https://www.optica.org/history/biographies/bios/mark_brongersma/ |website=Optica |access-date=May 14, 2025}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Brongersma was born in [[Geldrop|Geldrop, Netherlands]] in 1969.<ref>{{cite web | title=Smaller is key to solutions for Dutch researcher |publisher=Embassy of the Netherlands, Washington, DC | date=December 4, 2020 | url=https://nlintheusa.com/dr-mark-brongersma/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201217154358/https://nlintheusa.com/dr-mark-brongersma/ | archive-date=December 17, 2020 | url-status=dead}}</ref> He earned his Ph.D. in materials science in 1998 from [[Utrecht University]]'s FOM Institute [[AMOLF]] in Amsterdam, where he conducted research on light–matter interactions at the nanoscale. He then pursued postdoctoral studies at the [[California Institute of Technology]] from 1998 to 2001, being supervised by [[Harry Atwater]].<ref name=mse>{{cite web |title=Mark Brongersma |url=https://mse.stanford.edu/people/mark-brongersma |website=Stanford MSE |access-date=May 14, 2025}}</ref>

== Career ==
At Stanford, Brongersma leads a research group exploring new ways to manipulate light using nanoscale structures. His group focuses on metasurfaces, plasmonic devices, and atomically thin optical materials for sensing, imaging, and energy applications.<ref name=group>{{cite web |title=Brongersma Group |url=https://brongersma.stanford.edu/ |website=Stanford University |access-date=May 14, 2025}}</ref> He also serves as a faculty co-director of the Stanford Photonics Research Center (SPRC).<ref name=sprc>{{cite web |title=SPRC |url=https://photonics.stanford.edu |website=Stanford Photonics Research Center |access-date=May 14, 2025}}</ref>

His research demonstrated that metasurfaces can serve as scalable building blocks for optical systems, including transparent sensors and high-resolution imaging technologies.<ref name=publications>{{cite web |title=Selected Publications |url=https://brongersma.stanford.edu/publications/ |website=Brongersma Group |access-date=May 14, 2025}}</ref>

== Research contributions ==
* '''Plasmonics and Mie-tronics''': Brongersma coined the term "Mie-tronics" to describe optical phenomena in high-index dielectric nanostructures, expanding the field of plasmonics.<ref name=optica /><ref>{{cite journal |last=Won |first=Rachel |year=2019 |title=Into the 'Mie-tronic' era |journal=Nature Photonics |volume=13 |issue=9 |pages=585–587 |doi=10.1038/s41566-019-0512-5 |bibcode=2019NaPho..13..585W |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41566-019-0512-5|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* '''Optical Metasurfaces''': His team developed metasurface-based lenses and sensors for compact, efficient, and tunable optical systems.<ref name=publications />
* '''Atomically Thin Optics''': He used 2D materials in optical devices, exploiting excitonic effects at the atomic scale.<ref name=group />

== Publications and patents ==
Brongersma has authored more than 265 peer-reviewed articles.<ref name=stanford />

== Honors and awards ==
* National Science Foundation CAREER Award<ref name=stanford />
* Walter J. Gores Award for Excellence in Teaching at Stanford University<ref name=stanford />
* Raymond and Beverly [[Sackler Prize]] in the Physical Sciences for pioneering work in plasmonics<ref name=optica />

He is a Fellow of [[Optica (society)|Optica (formerly OSA)]], the [[Materials Research Society|Materials Research Society (MRS)]], [[SPIE]], and the [[American Physical Society|American Physical Society (APS)]].<ref name=optica />

== Industry impact ==
Brongersma co-founded Rolith Inc., a startup focused on nanostructured optical coatings and photonic devices. The company was acquired by Metamaterial Technologies Inc. in 2016.<ref>{{cite web |title=Metamaterial Technologies acquires Rolith |url=https://optics.org/news/7/6/2 |website=Optics.org |access-date=May 14, 2025}}</ref>
